topography.project_purpose: Liquid Staking. Structurally: 335 project-authored contract(s) across 13 chain(s); 28 ERC20 tokens, 6 ERC721 NFTs, 2 ERC1155 multi-tokens, 14 Chainlink feeds; role-gated via AccessControl; upgradeable via ERC1967/UUPS proxies; built on openzeppelin.
topography.relationship_narrative: The protocol comprises 3 functional families. Its contracts share 89 common project-authored base contract(s) (trustedcaller, erc165, motionsettings). Dominant framework: openzeppelin.

audits.report_name: The Lido protocol, from the very beginning, is built on trust in code, and that trust comes from careful and continuous verification. Every component of the Lido protocol has gone through multiple layers of independent review by leading blockchain security firms. Over the years, experts from Certora, MixBytes, Statemind, Ackee, OpenZeppelin Consensys Diligence, ChainSecurity, Oxorio, Hexens, and SigmaPrime have examined Lido protocol’s smart contracts, looking for ways to make them safer and more reliable. The results of these reviews are full audit reports and code-verification summaries, which are publicly available for anyone to explore [here]().
See [formal verification report]() for more details.
See [full report]() for more details. The report had been updated on 14 March 2023 with the build hashes of 4.1.0 release.
The implementation has been audited by MixBytes() and considered safe. Read the full report from [here]().

Review of fixes implemented for the zkSync L1ERC20Bridge (follow-up to the [August 2023 Cantina audit]()). No additional issues were identified.

There's a joint bug bounty for the vaults deployed at addresses listed in [the deployment verification audit record](). Any findings regarding the code deployed on those addresses can be reported to [the Lido Immunefi Bug bounty](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/lido/) with thresholds of up to $500k on critical finding.
The roles and addresses are listed in the following independent [report]() as of end of 2023.

audits_with_zero_matches.report_name: The Lido protocol, from the very beginning, is built on trust in code, and that trust comes from careful and continuous verification. Every component of the Lido protocol has gone through multiple layers of independent review by leading blockchain security firms. Over the years, experts from Certora, MixBytes, Statemind, Ackee, OpenZeppelin Consensys Diligence, ChainSecurity, Oxorio, Hexens, and SigmaPrime have examined Lido protocol’s smart contracts, looking for ways to make them safer and more reliable. The results of these reviews are full audit reports and code-verification summaries, which are publicly available for anyone to explore [here]().
See [full report]() for more details. The report had been updated on 14 March 2023 with the build hashes of 4.1.0 release.

There's a joint bug bounty for the vaults deployed at addresses listed in [the deployment verification audit record](). Any findings regarding the code deployed on those addresses can be reported to [the Lido Immunefi Bug bounty](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/lido/) with thresholds of up to $500k on critical finding.
The roles and addresses are listed in the following independent [report]() as of end of 2023.
